pharm: Selective beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist that relaxes detrusor smooth muscle during the bladder storage phase, increasing bladder capacity
quick: Start 25 mg once daily; may increase to max 50 mg once daily after 4-8 weeks
With or without food; swallow whole - do not chew, divide, or crush
No human data; animal studies showed fetal effects at high exposures
No human data; present in rat milk - likely present in human milk
Severe (eGFR 15-29): max 25 mg/day; ESRD or dialysis: not recommended
Moderate (Child-Pugh B): max 25 mg/day; severe (Child-Pugh C): not recommended
No specific interaction described in the label
Blood pressure periodically, especially in hypertensive patients
summary: Mirabegron is an oral, once-daily beta-3 adrenergic agonist for overactive bladder (OAB) in adults with urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency. By activating beta-3 receptors it relaxes the detrusor during bladder filling, increasing capacity. It can raise blood pressure and is not recommended in severe uncontrolled hypertension; it may also cause urinary retention in bladder outlet obstruction or with concomitant antimuscarinics, and rarely angioedema. As a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor it raises exposure to CYP2D6 substrates. Dose adjustment is required in severe renal and moderate hepatic impairment.
indications: Overactive bladder (OAB) in adults - treatment of urge urinary incontinence, urgency, and urinary frequency

dosage.d: 25 mg orally once daily; may increase to 50 mg once daily
dosage.t: Increase after 4 to 8 weeks if needed
dosage.n: 50 mg is the maximum recommended dose; extended-release tablets and the suspension are not interchangeable mg-for-mg

dosage.r: eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or requiring dialysis

admin: Swallow the extended-release tablet whole with water
Do not chew, divide, or crush
Take once daily with or without food
Extended-release tablets and extended-release oral suspension are different products and are not substitutable on a milligram-per-milligram basis
moa: Mirabegron is an agonist of the human beta-3 adrenergic receptor. By activating beta-3 receptors on the detrusor it relaxes bladder smooth muscle during the storage (filling) phase of the bladder fill-void cycle, increasing bladder capacity. It has very low intrinsic activity at human beta-1 and beta-2 receptors, although beta-1 stimulation has been seen in humans at a 200 mg dose (above the approved range).

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to mirabegron or any inactive ingredient of the tablet
relative: Severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >=180 and/or DBP >=110 mm Hg) - not recommended
Clinically significant bladder outlet obstruction - risk of urinary retention
Concomitant antimuscarinic OAB medications - risk of urinary retention
Use with narrow therapeutic index CYP2D6 substrates
Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) or ESRD/dialysis - not recommended
monitor: Blood pressure, especially in hypertensive patients
Signs and symptoms of urinary retention in bladder outlet obstruction or with antimuscarinics
Signs of angioedema, particularly upper airway involvement

preg: There are no studies of mirabegron in pregnant women to inform a drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse outcomes. In animals, administration during organogenesis caused reversible skeletal variations in rats at 22-fold the maximum recommended human dose (MRHD, by AUC) and decreased fetal body weights in rabbits at 14-fold the MRHD; at maternally toxic exposures, decreased fetal weight and increased fetal mortality (rats, 96-fold) and cardiac findings such as fetal cardiomegaly and dilated aortae (rabbits, 36-fold) were seen. The U.S. background risk of major birth defects is about 2-4% and of miscarriage about 15-20%.
lact: There are no data on the presence of mirabegron in human milk, its effects on the breastfed child, or effects on milk production. Mirabegron-related material was present in rat milk and in the stomachs of nursing pups after a single oral dose to lactating rats; when a drug is present in animal milk it is likely to be present in human milk. Weigh the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need for mirabegron and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed in mild or moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-89 mL/min/1.73 m2). In severe renal impairment (eGFR 15-29 mL/min/1.73 m2) the daily dose should not exceed 25 mg, reflecting roughly 92% higher Cmax and 118% higher AUC versus normal function. Mirabegron has not been studied in end-stage renal disease (eGFR <15) or in patients requiring dialysis and is not recommended in these populations.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed in mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A). In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class B) the daily dose should not exceed 25 mg, reflecting about 175% higher Cmax and 65% higher AUC versus normal function. Mirabegron has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class C) and is not recommended in this population.

major: Narrow therapeutic index CYP2D6 substrates (e.g. thioridazine, flecainide, propafenone) - increased exposure; monitor and adjust dose
Digoxin - mirabegron raised digoxin Cmax 29% and AUC 27%; start digoxin at its lowest dose and monitor serum levels
moderate: Metoprolol (CYP2D6 substrate) - mirabegron increased Cmax 90% and AUC 229%
Desipramine (CYP2D6 substrate) - mirabegron increased Cmax 79% and AUC 241%
Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole) - increased mirabegron Cmax 45% and AUC 80%
Antimuscarinic OAB drugs - additive urinary retention risk in obstruction
minor: Warfarin - single-dose study showed small increases (Cmax ~4%, AUC ~9%) with no effect on INR; multiple-dose effect not fully studied
Solifenacin, tamsulosin, oral contraceptives, rifampin - no dose adjustment needed
interactions.food: No clinically significant pharmacokinetic difference with or without food
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described in the label
interactions.diagnostics: As a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor mirabegron can increase exposure to CYP2D6 substrates; monitor and adjust narrow-index drugs and serum digoxin

common: Constipation, dry mouth, dizziness, back pain (Study 4)
serious: Increases in blood pressure (worsening of pre-existing hypertension)
Urinary retention (in bladder outlet obstruction or with antimuscarinics)
Angioedema of the face, lips, tongue, and/or larynx - may be life-threatening
Marked transaminase elevations (>10x baseline reported in 2 patients)
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome (single case at 100 mg with herbal co-medication)
emergency: Angioedema with upper airway swelling - discontinue and secure the airway

monitoring: Blood pressure periodically, especially in hypertensive patients
Signs and symptoms of urinary retention in patients with bladder outlet obstruction or on antimuscarinics
Signs of angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx)
Serum levels and effect of narrow-index CYP2D6 substrates and digoxin when co-prescribed
counsel: Take one tablet once daily; swallow whole with water and do not chew, divide, or crush it
May be taken with or without food
This medicine can raise blood pressure - monitor your blood pressure, particularly if you have hypertension, and report increases
Stop the drug and seek immediate care if you develop swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat or trouble breathing
Contact your clinician if you have difficulty emptying your bladder
Tell your clinician about all prescription, nonprescription, and herbal products, as doses may need adjustment
pk: Steady-state concentrations reached within 7 days of once-daily dosing
Maximum plasma concentration at about 3.5 hours; absolute bioavailability 29% (25 mg) to 35% (50 mg)
Once-daily dosing; steady-state exposure about double that of a single dose
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: First-in-class beta-3 adrenergic agonist for OAB - relaxes the detrusor during storage rather than blocking muscarinic receptors
Not recommended in severe uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >=180 and/or DBP >=110 mm Hg); monitor blood pressure
Moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor - watch metoprolol, desipramine, and other narrow-index CYP2D6 substrates
Cap at 25 mg/day in severe renal impairment or moderate hepatic impairment; avoid in ESRD/dialysis or Child-Pugh C
Extended-release tablets and the extended-release oral suspension are NOT interchangeable mg-for-mg
Angioedema can occur after the first dose or after multiple doses - counsel patients to recognize airway symptoms
missed: Take a missed dose as soon as you remember, unless more than 12 hours have passed since the missed dose. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the usual time. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Mirabegron has been given to healthy volunteers at single doses up to 400 mg, with palpitations and pulse rate over 100 bpm reported; multiple doses up to 300 mg/day for 10 days increased pulse rate and systolic blood pressure. Treatment of overdose should be symptomatic and supportive, with monitoring of pulse rate, blood pressure, and ECG.
